record.original_question: Classify transitive antilattices, where an antilattice N is transitive when its congruence lattice Con(N) is transitive, and a lattice L is transitive when for every pair of maximal chains a and b of L there is an automorphism of L that maps a to b.

evidence.quote: Let us call a lattice L transitive if for each pair of maximal chains a and b of L there exists an automorphism of L that maps one to the other one
We call an antilattice N transitive, if its congruence lattice Con(N ) is transitive.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An antilattice is an algebra $(N,\wedge,\vee)$ with two binary operations such that both $(N,\wedge)$ and $(N,\vee)$ are semigroups satisfying the absorption-failure axioms making $\wedge$ and $\vee$ anticommutative in the antilattice sense (i.e., $x\wedge y = x$ if and only if $y\wedge x = y$, and dually for $\vee$), so that no two distinct elements are comparable in either induced order. Let $\mathrm{Con}(N)$ denote the congruence lattice of $N$ as a universal algebra.

Call a lattice $L$ transitive if for every pair of maximal chains $a$ and $b$ of $L$ there exists an automorphism of $L$ mapping $a$ onto $b$. Call an antilattice $N$ transitive if its congruence lattice $\mathrm{Con}(N)$ is a transitive lattice in the above sense.

Problem: Classify, up to isomorphism, all transitive antilattices.
